name: Kahumamahon Saluan
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: (a) Stress. Stress (sometimes including secondary stress) is indicated in all cases where we have elicited a response, including cases where we reelicited words which originally appeared on someone else's wordlist. [...] In general, stress is non-phonemic, occurring on the penultimate syllable (but see the discussion below concerning long vowels, where indication of stress is significant). [...] (d) [...] Saluan contrasts the following in word final position: regular vowels, long vowels, and geminate vowels [...]. Long vowels are distinctive in that they do not attract stress, which falls on the preceding (viz. penultimate) syllable; [...] Compare: regular vowel: ˈsiku 'elbow' long vowel: ˈʔikuː 'tail' geminate vowels: tuˈmuːʔ 'live, grow'
new_statements.citation: Mead, David & Edy Pasanda. 2015. An initial appreciation of the dialect situation in Saluan and Batui (eastern Sulawesi, Indonesia). SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-013. Dallas: SIL International.
new_statements.locator: Appendix B, section B.1 'Transcription and presentation of wordlist responses', item (a) p.29 (PDF p.36) and item (d) p.30 (PDF p.37); wordlist SIM = Simpang I, 'Loinang (Kahumama'on)', B.3 p.32
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (+.txt;.. identical to../salu1253/ copy), Mead & Pasanda 2015, SIL ESR 2015-013. Locator verified with extracted text per page: PDF p.36 = printed p.29 carries Appendix B.1(a) 'Stress. Stress (sometimes including secondary stress) is indicated in all cases where we have elicited a response... In general, stress is non-phonemic, occurring on the penultimate syllable (but see the discussion below concerning long vowels, where indication of stress is significant).'; PDF p.37 = printed p.30 carries B.1(d) 'Long vowels are distinctive in that they do not attract stress, which falls on the preceding (viz. penultimate) syllable;... regular vowel: ˈsiku 'elbow' long vowel: ˈʔikuː 'tai…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Saluan word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable; a word-final long vowel counts as a single (final) syllable and does not draw stress (ˈʔikuː), while a final geminate/double vowel counts as two syllables so stress lands on its first half (tuˈmuːʔ = tumuuʔ). Stated for Saluan as a whole (survey of 11 Saluan wordlists incl. Simpang I = Kahumama'on); the Simpang items the authors re-elicited are stress-marked accordingly (ˈbutoŋ, poˈpokeʔ, siˈakan, ˈpalaː, moˈbosuː).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only that secondary stress was 'sometimes' marked in the authors' own transcriptions (e.g. ˌbahaŋˈkakak 'toad' in the Simpang list); no rule given.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final long vowels do not attract stress (stress stays penultimate counting the long vowel as one syllable); final geminate (double) vowels behave as two syllables. Authors also warn (B.1(i)) that differences in stress placement between wordlists from different transcribers may be mistranscriptions.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns isolated wordlist citation forms (488-item survey wordlists), i.e. word-level stress in elicitation; responses sometimes include enclitic -mo/-o or possessive -ɲo retained in transcription. It is a transcription note in a dialect-survey report, not a full phonological analysis, and is made for Saluan generally rather than for the Kahumama'on subdialect specifically.
new_statements.identity_note: kahu1242 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO 639-3 code [slb] 'Saluan, Kahumamahon', merged into [loe] Saluan in January 2008 on David Mead's Change Request 2007-118. Per that request and Mead & Pasanda 2015, 'Kahumamahon' denotes the Kahumama'on (Kohumama'on) subdialect of the Loinang (interior, n-dialect) dialect of Saluan, spoken in and around Simpang village(s), Bunta/Nuhon districts, Banggai Regency, Central Sulawesi; the real languoid is Saluan, glottocode salu1253. The quoted stress statement is Mead & Pasanda's general statement for Saluan; it rests on wordlists that include SIM = Simpang I 'Loinang (Kahumama'on)' (R. Brown 2001, items re-elicited and stress-marked by the authors, e.g. ˈbutoŋ, poˈpokeʔ, siˈakan, ˈpalaː, moˈbosuː), so it covers this variety first-hand, but it is not a Kahumama'on-specific phonology. A sibling audit for salu1253 already located the same passage; this entry would duplicate salu1253 in the catalog rather than add a distinct language.

sources.note: Appendix B.1(a) p.29: stress non-phonemic, on the penultimate syllable; B.1(d) p.30: word-final long vowels do not attract stress (stress stays on the preceding, penultimate syllable), whereas final geminate vowels count as two syllables (tuˈmuːʔ). Wordlists include SIM = Simpang I, Loinang (Kahumama'on), with authors' own stress marks on re-elicited items.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by David Mead). 2007. Change Request Number 2007-118: retire [slb] Saluan, Kahumamahon and merge into [loe] Saluan, Coastal (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International. 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; establishes identity: 'Kahumamahon' = Kohumama'on subdialect of the Loinang dialect of Saluan (Simpang village), one language with Coastal Saluan (all wordlists >80% lexical similarity; speakers regard it as a dialect of Saluan).
